meta.source: Hand-edited: Customs Tariff s. 24-52 and the List of Countries and Applicable Tariff Treatments (CBSA); HTSUS General Notes 3(c) and the special program indicators; CUSMA Chapter 4 and Annex 5-A
meta.note: The origin pre-check says whether a preference may be available and what proof it needs. Whether the goods qualify depends on the product-specific rule of origin, which DocCheck does not decide.

agreements.name: Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement (USMCA)
agreements.proof: Certification of origin with the nine minimum data elements of CUSMA Annex 5-A (on the invoice or a separate document)

agreements.name: Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership
agreements.proof: Certification of origin with the minimum data requirements of CPTPP Annex 3-B

agreements.name: Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement
agreements.proof: Origin declaration by the exporter on the invoice (CETA Annex 2), with the exporter's REX number for EU exporters

agreements.name: Canada-United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement
agreements.proof: Origin declaration by the exporter on the invoice

agreements.name: Canada-Colombia Free Trade Agreement
agreements.proof: Certificate of origin completed and signed by the exporter

agreements.name: United States-Colombia Trade Promotion Agreement
agreements.proof: Importer's claim based on a certification or knowledge that the goods are originating (19 CFR 10.3004)

cusmaHints.hint: Agricultural and food goods: most rules require the goods to be wholly obtained in the region or a change of chapter; check sugar and dairy restrictions.
Textiles and apparel: yarn-forward rule (yarn, fabric and cut-and-sew in the region), with a 10 % de minimis by weight of non-originating fibres.
Iron and steel goods: usually a change of heading or subheading; steel bought by vehicle producers must be melted and poured in North America.
Machinery and electrical goods: usually a change of tariff subheading, or a regional value content of 50 % (net cost) or 60 % (transaction value).
Vehicles and parts: regional value content of up to 75 %, labour value content and steel and aluminum purchase requirements (Appendix to Annex 4-B).

cusmaDefaultHint: Check the product-specific rule of origin for the subheading in CUSMA Annex 4-B (a change of tariff classification, a regional value content or both).
